facts.label: Version relationships and conflicts
facts.text: - Each 10-Q is a separate period report. The 10-K and the three 10-Qs are not duplicates of each other; each release is a management summary of the matching 10-Q period and does not replace it. - The 2026 10-Qs print 2025 comparatives that were reclassified: inventory impairment moved into cost of home sales revenues from the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-Q_2026-09-30 page:6), and stock-based compensation was added to adjusted EBITDA from the fourth quarter of 2025 with prior periods recast (page:66). The original 2025 Forms 10-Q are not in the pack, so 2025 quarterly figures exist only in this recast form. - Figure comparison between the Q3 2026 release and the Q3 2026 10-Q found no conflict: total liquidity $863.8 million in both (EX-99.1_2026-10-28 page:2; 10-Q_2026-09-30 page:52); homebuilding debt to capital 36.8% and net homebuilding debt to net capital 34.9% in both (page:66); net income $12.6 million in the release and $ 12,617 thousand in the statements (page:3). - Wording difference, not a numeric conflict: the Q1 2026 release says "$89.8 million of cash" while the Q2 and Q3 releases say cash "including cash equivalents and cash held in escrow". facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported financial base is complete enough for a credit view and shows clear deterioration. For the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, company-defined adjusted EBITDA was $294.366 million against $583.926 million in FY2024, and total debt at carrying value was $1,812.587 million against $1,476.213 million, so total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.16x and net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 5.87x, up from 2.53x and 2.27x. Both a lower earnings base and a higher revolver balance contribute: holding adjusted EBITDA at its FY2025 level, September 2026 debt alone gives 5.18x. Nine-month operating cash flow was negative $267.475 million, so inventory growth, share repurchases and dividends were financed by revolver borrowings. Liquidity of $744.0 million of undrawn revolver plus $86.086 million of cash and cash equivalents remains sizeable, the first bond maturity is August 2029, and the filings state covenant compliance, but covenant levels and headroom are not available in the sources, and the October 7, 2026 acquisition adds a cash call that the balance sheet does not yet reflect. The view is therefore a supported but restricted base: leverage and liquidity figures are firm, covenant headroom and post-acquisition leverage are not calculable.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: - EBITDA is net income before income tax expense, interest in cost of home sales revenues, other interest expense (income) and depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA further adds back inventory impairment, abandonment of lot option contracts, stock-based compensation, restructuring costs, loss on debt extinguishment, impairment on other investment and purchase price accounting for acquired work in process inventory (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:65). - Interest in cost of home sales revenues (60.738 in FY2025) is added back, because most interest is capitalized to inventory and expensed through cost of sales. EBITDA is therefore before most interest cost, and cash interest paid (81.3 in FY2025) is the better measure of the debt service burden. Interest incurred is close to cash interest in FY2025 (81.980 against 81.3). - Adjusted EBITDA adds back inventory impairment of 19.605 in the nine months of 2026, 21.816 in FY2025 and 8.778 in FY2024 (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:65); impairment appears in each period shown, so the unadjusted EBITDA ratios are shown alongside. - Adjusted EBITDA definitions changed: lot option abandonment was added from Q3 2025 and stock-based compensation from Q4 2025, with prior periods recast (10-K page:91, page:92; Q3 10-Q page:66). The FY2024, FY2025 and 2025 interim figures here use the recast definition, so the periods are comparable with each other but not with originally published 2024 or 2025 figures. - The revolver's "leverage ratio, as defined in the Credit Agreement" sets pricing (Q3 10-Q page:17). That definition is Not supplied and may differ from every ratio computed here.

facts.label: Interpretation
facts.text: - Evidence: LTM adjusted EBITDA of 294.366 is below FY2025 349.705 and FY2024 583.926, while total debt rose by 336.374 from 2024 year-end to September 2026. Mechanism: home sales gross margin fell (16.48% LTM against 21.49% in FY2024), and the 10-Q ties the latest impairment to higher incentives (Q3 10-Q page:21); a build in inventory (3,744.023 against 3,361.158 at year-end 2025, up 382.865) absorbs cash, and net revolver borrowings of 404.5 in the nine months (1,584.3 drawn less 1,179.8 repaid, Q3 10-Q page:3) rather than operating cash funded it. Implication: leverage on the company measure exceeds six times and net homebuilding debt to net capital has risen to 34.9% from 25.9%; further margin pressure or slower closings would raise leverage faster than debt reduction can occur. - Evidence: nine-month operating cash flow of negative 267.475 against negative 57.654 a year earlier, while dividends of 27.519 and repurchases of 71.198 continued. Mechanism: shareholder returns are discretionary but were paid while cash flow was negative. Implication: the flexibility to cut returns is a mitigant that the sources show has not yet been used. - Evidence: unsecured notes of 1,000.0 principal sit behind at least 320.716 of identified secured debt and share the guarantor group. Mechanism: effective subordination to secured claims at the guarantor level. Implication: bondholders rank behind secured construction and warehouse lenders, though these are small beside 4,790.025 of total assets. - Evidence: the first bond maturity is August 2029 and the revolver extends to 2030 for most commitments. Implication: no bond matures before August 2029; the near-term items are the repurchase facilities, which are self-liquidating against loans held for sale of 186.506, and construction loans. - Limitation: covenant headroom, post-acquisition leverage and cash interest for 2026 cannot be assessed from the sources, so the credit view is bounded by those gaps.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Century Communities, Inc. is a US single-family homebuilder that operates in 16 states and over 45 markets under two brands, Century Communities and Century Complete, with a captive mortgage, title, insurance and escrow business and a small multi-family rental development segment in Colorado. Revenue is almost wholly home sales, which depend on affordability, mortgage rates and the use of incentives; the company itself ties its latest price decline to incentives and its lower deliveries to slower absorption. The transaction that matters most to a creditor is the October 7, 2026 purchase of the assets of HistoryMaker Homes in Dallas for about $160.2 million of initial cash, which is a post-balance-sheet event that adds communities and deliveries but also a cash call whose funding is not stated, coming days after the September 30, 2026 revolver amendment that raised commitments to $1.2 billion. Ownership is public with no sponsor; the Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, who are brothers, hold a documented 13.9% stake and have employment agreements with change-of-control severance. No dividend recapitalisation, related-party leakage or creditor-adverse transaction is documented in the sources, but the proxy material and debt agreements that would show control rights, baskets and permitted payments are not supplied, so legal capacity is not assessed. The facts that move the credit most are demand and margin resilience, funding of the acquisition and shareholder returns while operating cash flow is negative, and the structural subordination of the unsecured notes to secured construction and warehouse debt.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The transaction of record after the balance sheet date is the acquisition, completed on October 7, 2026, of substantially all of the assets and certain liabilities of HMH Lifestyles, L.P., doing business as HistoryMaker Homes, a Dallas-area homebuilder, for initial cash consideration of approximately $160.2 million, subject to customary holdbacks and post-closing adjustments (Q3 10-Q page:7, page:34). It adds 29 active communities to the Texas segment (Q3 10-Q page:7). The company says it will increase its Dallas division's active communities from 12 to 41 as of September 30, 2026 and triple trailing-twelve-month deliveries from 211 to 669 homes, and its outlook includes 100 deliveries from the acquired business in the fourth quarter (Q3 release page:1, page:3); these are Management Language, not filed fact. The company also states it will keep a land relationship with HistoryMaker's sister land development company (Q3 release page:2). Because the deal closed after September 30, 2026, the acquired assets and assumed liabilities are not in the balance sheet, purchase accounting is incomplete, and the filing does not state how the cash consideration is funded. This is a subsequent event and it is kept out of every September 30, 2026 figure. Parties other than the target, any sponsor, a use-of-proceeds statement, and the effect on liquidity are Not supplied; the missing funding statement matters because revolver borrowings already stood at $456.0 million and nine-month operating cash flow was negative (financial base handoff).

facts.text: New debt and financing events are as follows. On September 30, 2026 the company signed the First Amendment to its Credit Agreement dated November 1, 2024 (administrative agent U.S. Bank National Association): commitments rose from $1.0 billion to $1.2 billion, maturity for participating extending lenders moved to November 1, 2030 with $100.0 million still maturing November 1, 2028, new lenders were added, certain financial covenants were revised, and the 0.10% credit spread adjustment was eliminated (Q3 10-Q page:16). The revised covenant terms are not supplied. In September 2025 the company issued $500.0 million of 6.625% senior notes due September 2033 and extinguished $500.0 million of 6.750% senior notes due 2027 at 100% of principal, for $511.4 million including accrued interest, with a loss on extinguishment of $1.4 million (10-K page:75). Earlier, the revolver was raised from $900.0 million to $1.0 billion on April 22, 2025 (10-K page:77). No new bond issue after September 2025 appears in the sources. The mortgage repurchase facilities, construction loans and revolver are described in the financial base handoff.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability and margin. Evidence: Q3 2026 average price down from 384.2 to 345.0 thousand and gross margin 15.0% against 17.9%, with the company citing incentives and slower absorption (Q3 10-Q page:35, page:37). Mechanic: price cuts fall straight to margin on a cost base that is partly fixed (selling, general and administrative expense rose to 14.1% of home sales revenue). Implication: earnings and cash flow are exposed to further rate rises; the leverage figures in the financial base already reflect lower earnings. Countering evidence: adjusted homebuilding gross margin of 19.3% and a stated backlog of 1,106 homes (Q3 10-Q page:37). - Cash conversion and liquidity. Evidence: operating cash outflow of 267.475 in nine months 2026 and inventory up to 3,744.023 (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:3). Mechanic: inventory is funded by the revolver, whose availability is subject to covenants that are not supplied. Implication: liquidity is adequate on reported figures but sensitive to the unpublished covenant tests and to the HistoryMaker cash call. - Acquisition and capital allocation. Evidence: repurchases that the company says it finances with cash and the revolver, and a 160.2 million acquisition seven days after a covenant amendment (Q3 10-Q page:7, page:16, page:62). Mechanic: external growth and returns compete with deleveraging. Implication: monitoring posture should follow post-acquisition leverage and any change in repurchase pace. The company has not shown a deleveraging plan in the sources (Insufficient Information). - Structural position. Evidence: unsecured notes guaranteed by operating subsidiaries and effectively subordinated to secured debt of the guarantors; Financial Services subsidiaries do not guarantee (Q3 10-Q page:49). Mechanic: warehouse and construction lenders have first claim on their collateral; recovery prospects for unsecured claims depend on inventory value realization, which this handoff does not conclude. - Concentration and sponsor alignment. Evidence: no customer concentration is given; the insider stake of 13.9% is documented (10-K page:48). Implication: owner-operator alignment is present; no sponsor.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Century Communities, Inc. has a weakened but still liquid credit profile in which earnings are falling faster than debt is being repaid. The strongest support is USD 744.0 million of undrawn revolver and USD 86.086 million of cash at 30 September 2026, no bond maturity before August 2029, and a 16-state footprint with a captive mortgage arm [CP-1; CP-1A]. The weakest point is leverage: total debt reached 6.16x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, from 2.53x in FY2024, while nine-month operating cash flow was negative USD 267.475 million and revolver borrowings funded inventory, buybacks and dividends. The outcome will be decided by covenant headroom, which the sources do not show, by how the USD 160.2 million HistoryMaker Homes purchase is funded, and by whether incentive-driven margin pressure eases.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Leverage has risen sharply on both a weaker earnings base and higher debt. Century Communities, Inc. reported total debt of USD 1,812.587 million at 30 September 2026 against last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 294.366 million, or 6.16x, and net debt of 5.87x, up from 2.53x and 2.27x in FY2024 (total leverage has more than doubled in under two years) and 4.13x and 3.81x in FY2025 [CP-1, Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the derived ratios]. Holding adjusted EBITDA at its FY2025 level, September 2026 debt alone gives 5.18x, so debt growth and earnings decline each contribute. On unadjusted EBITDA the ratios are 7.68x total and 7.31x net, because adjusted EBITDA adds back inventory impairment, which has occurred in every period shown. Implication: debt service capacity depends on a recovery in volume and margin rather than on deleveraging.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 2. Operating cash flow is negative and bank debt funds the gap. Net cash used in operating activities was USD 267.475 million in nine months 2026 against USD 57.654 million a year earlier, inventories rose by USD 382.865 million to USD 3,744.023 million, and the revolver balance rose from USD 51.5 million to USD 456.0 million (net drawings of USD 404.5 million) while still paying USD 27.519 million of dividends and USD 71.198 million of repurchases [CP-1; CP-1A, Documentary Fact]. Mechanic: homebuilding converts cash late, so growth in land and homes under construction absorbs liquidity ahead of closings. Implication: leverage on the company's own homebuilding measure rose to 34.9% net debt to net capital from 25.9%, and a slower sales pace would extend the cash outflow.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 3. Liquidity is adequate on reported figures, with a long bond runway. Undrawn revolver capacity was USD 744.0 million after the 30 September 2026 amendment raised commitments to USD 1.2 billion, and company-reported liquidity was USD 863.8 million including cash held in escrow [CP-1]. The first bond matures in August 2029 (USD 500.0 million), the next in September 2033 (USD 500.0 million), and USD 1.1 billion of revolver commitments run to November 2030. The near-term maturities are secured warehouse lines of USD 191.266 million through May 2027 and construction loans of USD 129.450 million from December 2026. Implication: refinancing risk for bondholders is back-ended, but revolver availability depends on covenants that are not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 4. Demand and margin are under pressure from incentives and rates. Third-quarter 2026 average selling price was USD 345.0 thousand against USD 384.2 thousand (down 10.2%), gross margin on home sales was 15.0% against 17.9%, deliveries were 2,442 against 2,486, and the company attributes the price decline to increased incentives and the volume decline to slower absorption, as management's explanation [CP-1A, Management Language]. Selling, general and administrative expense rose to 14.1% of home sales revenue from 12.6% on a partly fixed cost base. Mechanic: price cuts fall straight to earnings, and a large part of the customer base is entry-level buyers, whose demand is sensitive to affordability and mortgage rates [CP-1A, Documentary Fact]. Implication: the earnings base that supports leverage could fall further if rates rise.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile [Documentary Fact; CP-1]: USD 744.0 million undrawn on the revolver, USD 86.086 million of cash, no bond before August 2029, so near-term refinancing is limited to bank and warehouse lines. (2) Diversified operations [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: five regional homebuilding segments across 16 states, none above 25.0% of nine-month revenue, with Century Complete the largest, which limits single-market exposure. (3) Flexibility of land and cash use [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: about 45.1% of lots are controlled through options with obligations generally limited to deposits, and dividends and repurchases are discretionary. (4) Insider alignment [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: 13.9% ownership by the two senior executives. (5) Equity cushion [Documentary Fact; CP-1]: stockholders' equity of USD 2,560.998 million against total debt of USD 1,812.587 million.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) High and rising leverage [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]: 6.16x adjusted EBITDA and 7.68x unadjusted. spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-0 (source readiness) for Century Communities, Inc. (ticker CCS, issuer id ccs), as of 2026-11-05 with cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit_snapshot, public case. Reporting currency: USD. Current period: Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026). Prior period: FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025). Requested downstream modules: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5.

Question answered: can the seven pinned issuer sources support those modules, and what remains blocked or limited? This handoff gives source sufficiency only. It gives no credit conclusion and does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY. Statement amounts are printed in USD thousands; narrative text and releases print USD millions. The context file holds the user's dated settings, not issuer evidence. Its blank fields (deal terms, quotes, ratings, valuation inputs, sponsor, parent, borrower) are left blank, not read as zero.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

Hashes are the pinned sha256 of each retained text file. The first line of every file also prints a different sha256 for the original HTML text it was extracted from; the pinned value below is the one CP-OS verifies.

None. CP-0 is the first module of this run, so CP-OS supplied no upstream handoff.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases cover the annual report, three quarters and three earnings releases through September 30, 2026, and can support the four requested modules with bounded limitations. | Medium | The credit agreement, its amendments and the indentures are not in the pack, so covenant levels are not available. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited FY2025 statements and unaudited statements for each of the first three quarters of 2026 are present, with notes, debt tables and non-GAAP reconciliations. | Debt, liquidity and earnings work can be sourced from filed statements. | High |

| Covenant levels and headroom are not printed anywhere in the pack; the filings state only compliance, and the September 30, 2026 amendment revised financial covenants. | Covenant headroom cannot be assessed from this pack. | High |

| The acquisition of HistoryMaker Homes closed October 7, 2026, after the balance sheet date, with purchase accounting not finalized and no funding source stated. | Post-quarter leverage and liquidity are not in the reported balance sheet. | High |

| No presentations, ratings, market quotes or deal terms were supplied; earnings releases stand in for presentations, and text extraction cannot confirm charts or images. | Management claims rest on releases; external credit views are absent. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5. The pack holds the FY2025 Form 10-K, the Forms 10-Q for the quarters ended March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026, and the three matching earnings releases, all for the single registrant Century Communities, Inc., with a latest filing date of 2026-10-29 (per _retrieval.json) and therefore inside the 2026-11-05 cutoff. Filed statements control the facts; the releases are management documents that give attributed, supporting claims. The limitations are bounded and do not stop any consumer: the debt agreements are not supplied, no discrete fourth quarter 2025 statement exists in the pack, the October 7, 2026 acquisition is outside the reported balance sheet, and no image or chart content was inspected. None of these is a source-readiness BLOCK, and none makes a missing downstream handoff a condition. Source sufficiency is not completion of any downstream analysis.

Debt is tabulated at carrying value by instrument: 3.875% senior notes due August 2029, 6.625% senior notes due September 2033, construction loan agreements, other financing obligations, the revolving line of credit and the mortgage repurchase facilities, with total debt $ 1,812,587 at September 30, 2026 (10-Q_2026-09-30 page:14). Principal of each senior note is stated as $500.0 million (page:14, page:15).

- Earnings releases: they give quarter-based figures and attributed management narrative. The Q3 2026 release carries guidance (full-year 2026 deliveries of 9,350 to 9,650 homes and home sales revenues of $3.3 billion to $3.4 billion, EX-99.1_2026-10-28 page:3). Guidance is management's statement, not a filed fact.

- Legal and financing sources: no executed legal document is supplied. The Credit Agreement dated November 1, 2024 (10-K exhibit 10.10, page:101), the Incremental Joinder Agreement dated April 22, 2025 (10-K page:102), the First Amendment dated September 30, 2026 (10-Q_2026-09-30 page:73), and the indentures dated August 23, 2021 and September 17, 2025 (10-K page:100) appear only as exhibit references incorporated by reference. They are separate active sources that are absent, not collapsed into the filings. The context field legal_documents reads "none", which agrees.

- Workbooks: none supplied. Scans, images and decks: none supplied. The pack contains no presentations; the three releases replace them. Text extraction cannot support any claim of chart or image inspection, so none is made.
### Version relationships and conflicts
- Each 10-Q is a separate period report. The 10-K and the three 10-Qs are not duplicates of each other; each release is a management summary of the matching 10-Q period and does not replace it.

- The 2026 10-Qs print 2025 comparatives that were reclassified: inventory impairment moved into cost of home sales revenues from the fourth quarter of 2025 (10-Q_2026-09-30 page:6), and stock-based compensation was added to adjusted EBITDA from the fourth quarter of 2025 with prior periods recast (page:66). The original 2025 Forms 10-Q are not in the pack, so 2025 quarterly figures exist only in this recast form.

- Figure comparison between the Q3 2026 release and the Q3 2026 10-Q found no conflict: total liquidity $863.8 million in both (EX-99.1_2026-10-28 page:2; 10-Q_2026-09-30 page:52); homebuilding debt to capital 36.8% and net homebuilding debt to net capital 34.9% in both (page:66); net income $12.6 million in the release and $ 12,617 thousand in the statements (page:3).

- Wording difference, not a numeric conflict: the Q1 2026 release says "$89.8 million of cash" while the Q2 and Q3 releases say cash "including cash equivalents and cash held in escrow". The Q1 10-Q balance sheet prints cash and cash equivalents $ 78,182 and cash held in escrow $ 11,621 (10-Q_2026-03-31 page:2), so the Q1 release figure is the combined measure. Downstream modules must use the 10-Q definition.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Reported leverage rose sharply while earnings fell. Total debt to adjusted EBITDA went from 2.53x in FY2024 to 6.16x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, though liquidity of $863.8 million remains. | Medium | Covenant levels are not in the sources, and cash interest paid is disclosed only for full years. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Adjusted EBITDA fell to $294.366 million for the last twelve months from $583.926 million in FY2024, while total debt rose to $1,812.587 million. | Debt now exceeds six times adjusted EBITDA on the company definition. | High |

| Revolver borrowings rose to $456.0 million from $51.5 million at year-end 2025 as nine-month operating cash flow was negative $267.475 million. | Growth in inventory is being funded with floating-rate bank debt. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 7.40x in FY2024 and 4.30x in FY2025; no cash interest figure exists for the nine months of 2026. | Recent coverage cannot be stated on a cash basis. | Medium |

| The first bond maturity is $500.0 million in August 2029, and the revolver was extended in part to November 2030. | No bond refinancing falls before 2029; bank and warehouse lines carry near-term maturities. | High |

| The acquisition of HistoryMaker Homes for about $160.2 million cash closed October 7, 2026, after the balance sheet date. | Reported September figures understate post-quarter funding needs. | High |
### Financial base view

The reported financial base is complete enough for a credit view and shows clear deterioration. For the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, company-defined adjusted EBITDA was $294.366 million against $583.926 million in FY2024, and total debt at carrying value was $1,812.587 million against $1,476.213 million, so total debt to adjusted EBITDA is 6.16x and net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 5.87x, up from 2.53x and 2.27x. Both a lower earnings base and a higher revolver balance contribute: holding adjusted EBITDA at its FY2025 level, September 2026 debt alone gives 5.18x. Nine-month operating cash flow was negative $267.475 million, so inventory growth, share repurchases and dividends were financed by revolver borrowings. Liquidity of $744.0 million of undrawn revolver plus $86.086 million of cash and cash equivalents remains sizeable, the first bond maturity is August 2029, and the filings state covenant compliance, but covenant levels and headroom are not available in the sources, and the October 7, 2026 acquisition adds a cash call that the balance sheet does not yet reflect. The view is therefore a supported but restricted base: leverage and liquidity figures are firm, covenant headroom and post-acquisition leverage are not calculable.

### Liquidity and covenants

Company-reported liquidity was 863.8 at 2026-09-30 against about 1.1 billion at 2025-12-31 (Q3 10-Q page:52). It is defined as cash and cash equivalents plus cash held in escrow plus current revolver capacity, so it includes escrow of 33.740 that this handoff excludes from cash. Undrawn committed capacity is the revolver only (744.0). Excluded: the construction loans, which have 10.650 of the 140.1 commitments undrawn but only for specified multi-family projects; and the mortgage repurchase facilities, with 108.734 of 300.0 unused, of which only the Truist line is committed and the split is not printed. Within twelve months of 2026-09-30, the repurchase facilities (through May 28, 2027) and construction loans maturing from December 31, 2026 fall due; neither the revolver nor the notes do.

Covenants: the filings state compliance with all covenants under the senior notes, revolver, construction loans and repurchase facilities (Q3 10-Q page:56), and the September 30, 2026 First Amendment revised certain financial covenants (Q3 10-Q page:16). The maintenance tests, their levels, step-downs and the issuer's reported covenant figures are Not supplied, because the Credit Agreement, the First Amendment and the indentures are not in the pack. Headroom is therefore Not calculable. The company-printed net homebuilding debt to net capital of 34.9% is a company non-GAAP metric, not a stated covenant.
### Latest quarter and subsequent events
- Q3 2026 results: total revenues 864.467 against 980.284 in Q3 2025; net income 12.617 against 37.403; adjusted EBITDA 63.412 against 87.740, down 27.7% as printed (Q3 10-Q page:3, page:65).
- Inventory impairment of 19.605 in Q3 2026 on six communities with carrying value 62.3 before impairment, driven by higher incentives to improve absorptions (Q3 10-Q page:21).

- Financing: the September 30, 2026 First Amendment raised revolver commitments from 1.0 billion to 1.2 billion, extended maturity to November 1, 2030 for participating lenders, added lenders, revised certain financial covenants and removed the 0.10% credit spread adjustment (Q3 10-Q page:16). Revolver drawings rose to 456.0 from 329.6 at 2026-06-30 (Q2 10-Q page:13; Q3 10-Q page:14).
- Capital returns in Q3 2026: 169,903 shares repurchased for 11.6 and dividends of 0.32 per share (9.052 declared) (Q3 10-Q page:25, page:62, page:63).

- Subsequent event: on October 7, 2026 the company acquired substantially all assets of HMH Lifestyles, L.P. (HistoryMaker Homes) for initial cash consideration of approximately 160.2, subject to holdbacks and closing adjustments, adding 29 active communities in Texas. Purchase accounting is incomplete and the funding source is not stated (Q3 10-Q page:7).

- Management outlook (attributed, not a filed fact): full-year 2026 deliveries of 9,350 to 9,650 homes including 100 from HistoryMaker, and home sales revenues of 3.3 billion to 3.4 billion (Q3 release page:3).
### Definition review

- EBITDA is net income before income tax expense, interest in cost of home sales revenues, other interest expense (income) and depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA further adds back inventory impairment, abandonment of lot option contracts, stock-based compensation, restructuring costs, loss on debt extinguishment, impairment on other investment and purchase price accounting for acquired work in process inventory (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:65).

- Interest in cost of home sales revenues (60.738 in FY2025) is added back, because most interest is capitalized to inventory and expensed through cost of sales. EBITDA is therefore before most interest cost, and cash interest paid (81.3 in FY2025) is the better measure of the debt service burden. Interest incurred is close to cash interest in FY2025 (81.980 against 81.3).

- Adjusted EBITDA adds back inventory impairment of 19.605 in the nine months of 2026, 21.816 in FY2025 and 8.778 in FY2024 (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:65); impairment appears in each period shown, so the unadjusted EBITDA ratios are shown alongside.

- Adjusted EBITDA definitions changed: lot option abandonment was added from Q3 2025 and stock-based compensation from Q4 2025, with prior periods recast (10-K page:91, page:92; Q3 10-Q page:66). The FY2024, FY2025 and 2025 interim figures here use the recast definition, so the periods are comparable with each other but not with originally published 2024 or 2025 figures.
- The revolver's "leverage ratio, as defined in the Credit Agreement" sets pricing (Q3 10-Q page:17). That definition is Not supplied and may differ from every ratio computed here.
### Interpretation

- Evidence: LTM adjusted EBITDA of 294.366 is below FY2025 349.705 and FY2024 583.926, while total debt rose by 336.374 from 2024 year-end to September 2026. Mechanism: home sales gross margin fell (16.48% LTM against 21.49% in FY2024), and the 10-Q ties the latest impairment to higher incentives (Q3 10-Q page:21); a build in inventory (3,744.023 against 3,361.158 at year-end 2025, up 382.865) absorbs cash, and net revolver borrowings of 404.5 in the nine months (1,584.3 drawn less 1,179.8 repaid, Q3 10-Q page:3) rather than operating cash funded it. Implication: leverage on the company measure exceeds six times and net homebuilding debt to net capital has risen to 34.9% from 25.9%; further margin pressure or slower closings would raise leverage faster than debt reduction can occur.

- Evidence: nine-month operating cash flow of negative 267.475 against negative 57.654 a year earlier, while dividends of 27.519 and repurchases of 71.198 continued. Mechanism: shareholder returns are discretionary but were paid while cash flow was negative. Implication: the flexibility to cut returns is a mitigant that the sources show has not yet been used.

- Evidence: unsecured notes of 1,000.0 principal sit behind at least 320.716 of identified secured debt and share the guarantor group. Mechanism: effective subordination to secured claims at the guarantor level. Implication: bondholders rank behind secured construction and warehouse lenders, though these are small beside 4,790.025 of total assets.

- Evidence: the first bond maturity is August 2029 and the revolver extends to 2030 for most commitments. Implication: no bond matures before August 2029; the near-term items are the repurchase facilities, which are self-liquidating against loans held for sale of 186.506, and construction loans.
- Limitation: covenant headroom, post-acquisition leverage and cash interest for 2026 cannot be assessed from the sources, so the credit view is bounded by those gaps.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Century Communities is a publicly held, geographically spread US homebuilder with a captive mortgage arm. Demand pressure, rising incentives and a debt-funded acquisition drive the credit story, and no sponsor or related-party leakage is documented. | Medium | No debt agreements, ratings or proxy material are in the sources, so control rights and creditor protections cannot be assessed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

### Business and transaction view

Century Communities, Inc. is a US single-family homebuilder that operates in 16 states and over 45 markets under two brands, Century Communities and Century Complete, with a captive mortgage, title, insurance and escrow business and a small multi-family rental development segment in Colorado. Revenue is almost wholly home sales, which depend on affordability, mortgage rates and the use of incentives; the company itself ties its latest price decline to incentives and its lower deliveries to slower absorption. The transaction that matters most to a creditor is the October 7, 2026 purchase of the assets of HistoryMaker Homes in Dallas for about $160.2 million of initial cash, which is a post-balance-sheet event that adds communities and deliveries but also a cash call whose funding is not stated, coming days after the September 30, 2026 revolver amendment that raised commitments to $1.2 billion. Ownership is public with no sponsor; the Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, who are brothers, hold a documented 13.9% stake and have employment agreements with change-of-control severance. No dividend recapitalisation, related-party leakage or creditor-adverse transaction is documented in the sources, but the proxy material and debt agreements that would show control rights, baskets and permitted payments are not supplied, so legal capacity is not assessed. The facts that move the credit most are demand and margin resilience, funding of the acquisition and shareholder returns while operating cash flow is negative, and the structural subordination of the unsecured notes to secured construction and warehouse debt.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction of record after the balance sheet date is the acquisition, completed on October 7, 2026, of substantially all of the assets and certain liabilities of HMH Lifestyles, L.P., doing business as HistoryMaker Homes, a Dallas-area homebuilder, for initial cash consideration of approximately $160.2 million, subject to customary holdbacks and post-closing adjustments (Q3 10-Q page:7, page:34). It adds 29 active communities to the Texas segment (Q3 10-Q page:7). The company says it will increase its Dallas division's active communities from 12 to 41 as of September 30, 2026 and triple trailing-twelve-month deliveries from 211 to 669 homes, and its outlook includes 100 deliveries from the acquired business in the fourth quarter (Q3 release page:1, page:3); these are Management Language, not filed fact. The company also states it will keep a land relationship with HistoryMaker's sister land development company (Q3 release page:2). Because the deal closed after September 30, 2026, the acquired assets and assumed liabilities are not in the balance sheet, purchase accounting is incomplete, and the filing does not state how the cash consideration is funded. This is a subsequent event and it is kept out of every September 30, 2026 figure. Parties other than the target, any sponsor, a use-of-proceeds statement, and the effect on liquidity are Not supplied; the missing funding statement matters because revolver borrowings already stood at $456.0 million and nine-month operating cash flow was negative (financial base handoff).

New debt and financing events are as follows. On September 30, 2026 the company signed the First Amendment to its Credit Agreement dated November 1, 2024 (administrative agent U.S. Bank National Association): commitments rose from $1.0 billion to $1.2 billion, maturity for participating extending lenders moved to November 1, 2030 with $100.0 million still maturing November 1, 2028, new lenders were added, certain financial covenants were revised, and the 0.10% credit spread adjustment was eliminated (Q3 10-Q page:16). The revised covenant terms are not supplied. In September 2025 the company issued $500.0 million of 6.625% senior notes due September 2033 and extinguished $500.0 million of 6.750% senior notes due 2027 at 100% of principal, for $511.4 million including accrued interest, with a loss on extinguishment of $1.4 million (10-K page:75). Earlier, the revolver was raised from $900.0 million to $1.0 billion on April 22, 2025 (10-K page:77). No new bond issue after September 2025 appears in the sources. The mortgage repurchase facilities, construction loans and revolver are described in the financial base handoff.

### Conflicts and logged differences

- Century Complete geography: the 10-K lists Century Complete states as "Alabama, Arizona, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, North Carolina, and South Carolina" (10-K page:6), while the Q3 10-Q lists "Alabama, Arizona, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Nevada, North Carolina, and South Carolina" and states operations in 10 states (Q3 10-Q page:8). Logged, not reconciled; the sources do not say whether Nevada was added in 2026 or omitted earlier. Effect: state-level concentration for the Century Complete segment cannot be fixed.

- Cash definition: the Q1 release describes "$89.8 million of cash" while later releases say cash including cash equivalents and cash held in escrow (Q1 release page:2; Q2 release page:2). The Q1 10-Q balance sheet shows 78,182 and 11,621 (US$ thousands) (Q1 10-Q page:2). Noted in the source-readiness handoff; the filing governs.
- No other conflict was found between the releases and the Forms 10-Q on the figures compared (liquidity, ratios, deliveries).
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability and margin. Evidence: Q3 2026 average price down from 384.2 to 345.0 thousand and gross margin 15.0% against 17.9%, with the company citing incentives and slower absorption (Q3 10-Q page:35, page:37). Mechanic: price cuts fall straight to margin on a cost base that is partly fixed (selling, general and administrative expense rose to 14.1% of home sales revenue). Implication: earnings and cash flow are exposed to further rate rises; the leverage figures in the financial base already reflect lower earnings. Countering evidence: adjusted homebuilding gross margin of 19.3% and a stated backlog of 1,106 homes (Q3 10-Q page:37).

- Cash conversion and liquidity. Evidence: operating cash outflow of 267.475 in nine months 2026 and inventory up to 3,744.023 (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:3). Mechanic: inventory is funded by the revolver, whose availability is subject to covenants that are not supplied. Implication: liquidity is adequate on reported figures but sensitive to the unpublished covenant tests and to the HistoryMaker cash call.

- Acquisition and capital allocation. Evidence: repurchases that the company says it finances with cash and the revolver, and a 160.2 million acquisition seven days after a covenant amendment (Q3 10-Q page:7, page:16, page:62). Mechanic: external growth and returns compete with deleveraging. Implication: monitoring posture should follow post-acquisition leverage and any change in repurchase pace. - Structural position. Evidence: unsecured notes guaranteed by operating subsidiaries and effectively subordinated to secured debt of the guarantors; Financial Services subsidiaries do not guarantee (Q3 10-Q page:49). Mechanic: warehouse and construction lenders have first claim on their collateral; recovery prospects for unsecured claims depend on inventory value realization, which this handoff does not conclude.

- Concentration and sponsor alignment. Evidence: no customer concentration is given; the insider stake of 13.9% is documented (10-K page:48). Implication: owner-operator alignment is present; no sponsor.

Fundamental credit synthesis for Century Communities, Inc. (ticker CCS, issuer id ccs), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. It combines the financial base [CP-1] and the business and transaction context [CP-1A] for the consolidated registrant, in USD, with current period Q3 2026 and prior period FY2025.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs
This module takes no new source text; it works only from the upstream handoffs below. The issuer sources those handoffs rely on are listed for completeness.

| 10-K_2025-12-31_ccs-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl | 40822bca77f3d1f280fa9bdb025667cff0a3cbada92f0367c2ce2aea0f14cd10 |

### Handoffs relied on
| Module | Pinned sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | c251b67407b3993cf09de40f1b6adea510b7bad7bb25a2815575a608bae15041 | Source readiness and inherited limitations. |
| CP-1 | deba02fbf78513edd8848cc803441953597a0770ce39b23fafaf06d522a04d21 | Financial base: leverage, interest cover, liquidity, maturities, capital structure. |
| CP-1A | 0d321ce4e4e6edfb589c2f39b96943e74f895ae8f426b8382a22e2742976563a | Business model, transaction, ownership and governance rows. |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Century Communities has a weakened but liquid credit profile: leverage is 6.16x adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow is negative, offset by USD 744.0 million of undrawn revolver and no bond maturity before August 2029. | Medium | Covenant levels, post-acquisition funding and 2026 cash interest are not in the sources. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Total debt was 6.16x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, against 4.13x in FY2025 and 2.53x in FY2024. | Leverage has more than doubled in under two years. | High |

| Operating cash flow was negative USD 267.475 million in nine months 2026 while the revolver rose from USD 51.5 million to USD 456.0 million. | Inventory growth and shareholder returns are being funded by floating-rate bank debt. | High |

| Average selling price fell 10.2% in Q3 2026 on higher incentives, and homebuilding gross margin was 15.0% against 17.9%. | Earnings are exposed to further rate increases and incentive costs. | High |
| The USD 160.2 million HistoryMaker Homes acquisition closed after quarter-end and its funding is not stated. | Post-quarter leverage and liquidity cannot yet be measured. | High |
### Credit view

Century Communities, Inc. has a weakened but still liquid credit profile in which earnings are falling faster than debt is being repaid. The strongest support is USD 744.0 million of undrawn revolver and USD 86.086 million of cash at 30 September 2026, no bond maturity before August 2029, and a 16-state footprint with a captive mortgage arm [CP-1; CP-1A]. The weakest point is leverage: total debt reached 6.16x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, from 2.53x in FY2024, while nine-month operating cash flow was negative USD 267.475 million and revolver borrowings funded inventory, buybacks and dividends. The outcome will be decided by covenant headroom, which the sources do not show, by how the USD 160.2 million HistoryMaker Homes purchase is funded, and by whether incentive-driven margin pressure eases.
### Credit assessment
| Item | Content | Category | Confidence |

| Assessment | The company has adequate reported liquidity and a long bond maturity runway, but its leverage, negative operating cash flow and falling margins make the credit weaker than in FY2024. The view rests on filed figures [CP-1] and documented business facts [CP-1A]. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |

| Thesis | Liquidity and a back-ended bond ladder protect against near-term refinancing stress, but weaker earnings and bank-funded growth reduce the margin for error. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |

| Why not High | Covenant tests, acquisition funding, 2026 cash interest and ratings are not supplied, and the business-context handoff judges this module ready only with limitations [CP-1A; CP-0]. | Insufficient Information | Not applicable |
### Key findings

1. Leverage has risen sharply on both a weaker earnings base and higher debt. Century Communities, Inc. reported total debt of USD 1,812.587 million at 30 September 2026 against last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 294.366 million, or 6.16x, and net debt of 5.87x, up from 2.53x and 2.27x in FY2024 (total leverage has more than doubled in under two years) and 4.13x and 3.81x in FY2025 [CP-1, Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the derived ratios]. Holding adjusted EBITDA at its FY2025 level, September 2026 debt alone gives 5.18x, so debt growth and earnings decline each contribute. On unadjusted EBITDA the ratios are 7.68x total and 7.31x net, because adjusted EBITDA adds back inventory impairment, which has occurred in every period shown. Implication: debt service capacity depends on a recovery in volume and margin rather than on deleveraging.

2. Operating cash flow is negative and bank debt funds the gap. Net cash used in operating activities was USD 267.475 million in nine months 2026 against USD 57.654 million a year earlier, inventories rose by USD 382.865 million to USD 3,744.023 million, and the revolver balance rose from USD 51.5 million to USD 456.0 million (net drawings of USD 404.5 million) while still paying USD 27.519 million of dividends and USD 71.198 million of repurchases [CP-1; CP-1A, Documentary Fact]. Mechanic: homebuilding converts cash late, so growth in land and homes under construction absorbs liquidity ahead of closings. Implication: leverage on the company's own homebuilding measure rose to 34.9% net debt to net capital from 25.9%, and a slower sales pace would extend the cash outflow.

3. Liquidity is adequate on reported figures, with a long bond runway. Undrawn revolver capacity was USD 744.0 million after the 30 September 2026 amendment raised commitments to USD 1.2 billion, and company-reported liquidity was USD 863.8 million including cash held in escrow [CP-1]. The first bond matures in August 2029 (USD 500.0 million), the next in September 2033 (USD 500.0 million), and USD 1.1 billion of revolver commitments run to November 2030. The near-term maturities are secured warehouse lines of USD 191.266 million through May 2027 and construction loans of USD 129.450 million from December 2026. Implication: refinancing risk for bondholders is back-ended, but revolver availability depends on covenants that are not supplied.

4. Demand and margin are under pressure from incentives and rates. Third-quarter 2026 average selling price was USD 345.0 thousand against USD 384.2 thousand (down 10.2%), gross margin on home sales was 15.0% against 17.9%, deliveries were 2,442 against 2,486, and the company attributes the price decline to increased incentives and the volume decline to slower absorption, as management's explanation [CP-1A, Management Language]. Selling, general and administrative expense rose to 14.1% of home sales revenue from 12.6% on a partly fixed cost base. Mechanic: price cuts fall straight to earnings, and a large part of the customer base is entry-level buyers, whose demand is sensitive to affordability and mortgage rates [CP-1A, Documentary Fact]. Implication: the earnings base that supports leverage could fall further if rates rise.

5. Interest cover has weakened, with only annual cash interest available. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 7.40x in FY2024 and 4.30x in FY2025; for the last twelve months only an accrual proxy of 3.62x exists, because cash interest for 2026 is not disclosed [CP-1, Analyst Interpretation]. Most interest is capitalized to inventory and recognized through cost of sales, so EBITDA is stated before most interest cost. Implication: coverage is declining, and the recent trend cannot be confirmed on a cash basis.

6. The HistoryMaker Homes acquisition adds a cash call outside the reported balance sheet. The company bought the business on 7 October 2026 for initial cash consideration of about USD 160.2 million, adding 29 Texas communities, and the filing does not state how it is funded [CP-1A, Documentary Fact; the Dallas community and delivery targets are Management Language]. Implication: reported September leverage and liquidity understate the position after the deal, and the revolver is the likely but unconfirmed source.

7. Governance is aligned but capital returns continued as borrowing rose. The Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, who are brothers, held 13.9% of shares at 31 December 2025; no related-party leakage, dividend recapitalisation or creditor-adverse transaction is documented, and the company says repurchases use cash and the revolver [CP-1A, Documentary Fact]. Implication: the behaviour reads as Neutral or Mixed, with discretion to cut returns still unused.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile [Documentary Fact; CP-1]: USD 744.0 million undrawn on the revolver, USD 86.086 million of cash, no bond before August 2029, so near-term refinancing is limited to bank and warehouse lines. (2) Diversified operations [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: five regional homebuilding segments across 16 states, none above 25.0% of nine-month revenue, with Century Complete the largest, which limits single-market exposure. (3) Flexibility of land and cash use [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: about 45.1% of lots are controlled through options with obligations generally limited to deposits, and dividends and repurchases are discretionary. (4) Insider alignment [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: 13.9% ownership by the two senior executives. (5) Equity cushion [Documentary Fact; CP-1]: stockholders' equity of USD 2,560.998 million against total debt of USD 1,812.587 million.

Weaknesses. (1) High and rising leverage [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]: 6.16x adjusted EBITDA and 7.68x unadjusted. (2) Negative operating cash flow [Documentary Fact; CP-1]: bank-funded growth and returns. (3) Margin compression [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: price cuts via incentives on a partly fixed cost base. (4) Floating-rate bank dependence [Documentary Fact; CP-1]: the revolver of USD 456.0 million, repurchase facilities and construction loans carry floating rates, and the revolver's covenants are not visible. (5) Acquisition and capital allocation [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]: a USD 160.2 million cash purchase while the company continued buybacks, with funding unstated. (6) Structural subordination [Documentary Fact; CP-1]: unsecured notes sit behind at least USD 320.716 million of identified secured debt and the non-guarantor mortgage subsidiary's lines.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Leverage and earnings compression | Lower price and volume reduce EBITDA on a partly fixed cost base while debt rose [CP-1; CP-1A] | Leverage could exceed the current 6.16x if earnings fall further | Material |
| Cash burn funded by floating-rate bank debt | Inventory build and shareholder returns exceed operating cash [CP-1] | Higher interest cost and greater reliance on revolver availability | Material |
| Rate and incentive sensitivity of demand | Entry-level buyers and adjustable-rate mortgage use make demand sensitive to rates [CP-1A] | Further price cuts and impairments | Material |
| Acquisition funding and integration | USD 160.2 million cash call with unstated funding [CP-1A] | Post-deal leverage and liquidity are unmeasured | Material |
| Covenant headroom unknown | Revolver amendment revised covenants; levels not supplied [CP-1] | Availability could tighten without notice; not assessable here | Material |
| Structural subordination | Secured construction and warehouse debt ranks ahead at subsidiary level [CP-1] | Unsecured claims sit behind these lenders; no recovery conclusion is drawn | Minor |
| Century Living exit | Multi-family inventory financed by construction loans pending disposal [CP-1A] | Exit timing and price are undisclosed | Minor |
## Calculations

No new calculation was made. Every figure is taken from the financial base [CP-1] or the business context [CP-1A] as stated there, including the derived ratios, whose inputs and formulas are shown in the financial base handoff.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | What it affects | Action |

| Covenant tests, levels and headroom; executed Credit Agreement, First Amendment and indentures not supplied | High | Liquidity reliability, creditor control and legal capacity | Obtain executed agreements. |
| Funding source and purchase accounting for the HistoryMaker Homes acquisition; no pro forma figures | Medium | Post-quarter leverage and liquidity | Use Q4 2026 filings. |
| Cash interest paid for 2026 not disclosed | Medium | Interest cover for the last twelve months | Use the next annual report. |
| Letters of credit of USD 42.3 million not allocated to facilities | Medium | Revolver availability | Confirm allocation. |
| Ratings, market quotes and deal terms not in context | Low | External cross-check | Supply if needed. |
| No proxy statement; control rights and related-party detail not supplied | Medium | Governance assessment | Obtain the proxy statement. |

| Upstream readiness: business-context handoff judges this module ready with limitations; inherited limitations from the source-readiness handoff apply | Medium | Confidence capped below High | Resolve the gaps above. |

CP-5, the evidence trace validator, should check each figure in this synthesis against the financial base and the business context, and in particular trace the leverage ratios, the nine-month cash flow and revolver figures, and the HistoryMaker Homes terms to their source pages.
